prompt: Which three table settings cannot be changed after a Dataverse table is created? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Schema name
Table type
Table ownership
Primary column name
Attachments setting

explanation: Schema-Name, Tabellentyp (Standard, Activity, Virtual, Elastic) und Besitzverhältnis (User or Team bzw. Organization) sind nach dem Anlegen fix. Anzeigename und Beschreibung lassen sich dagegen jederzeit ändern — deshalb müssen die drei unveränderlichen Angaben vor dem Erstellen stimmen.

source.title: Table characteristics
source.quote: The following settings can't be changed after creation: Schema name Table type Table ownership

prompt: Match each Dataverse custom table type to its description.

right.text: Default table type for most use cases
Used for records with time-bound interactions, such as tasks or calls
External data presented as if native to Dataverse
High-scale tables powered by Azure Cosmos DB, for datasets with tens of millions of rows

explanation: Standard ist der Regelfall. Activity-Tabellen halten zeitgebundene Interaktionen wie Aufgaben oder Anrufe. Virtual-Tabellen zeigen externe Daten, als lägen sie in Dataverse. Elastic-Tabellen laufen auf Azure Cosmos DB und sind für zweistellige Millionen-Zeilenzahlen gedacht.

source.title: Table characteristics
source.quote: Standard: Default table type for most use cases Activity: Used for records with time-bound interactions (e.g., tasks, calls) Virtual: External data presented as if native to Dataverse Elastic: High-scale tables powered by Azure Cosmos DB, suitable for datasets with tens of millions of rows

prompt: What uniquely identifies a row in a Dataverse table, and what is the primary column used for?

options.text: A GUID is the primary key; the primary column is a readable text field shown in apps and flows
The primary column is the primary key, and the GUID is kept for audit history alone
An auto-incrementing integer is the primary key; the primary column stores the row owner
Both the GUID and the primary column must be entered by the user when a row is created

explanation: Dataverse erzeugt beim Anlegen einer Zeile automatisch eine GUID als Primärschlüssel. Zusätzlich hat jede Tabelle eine Primärspalte — ein lesbares Textfeld, das Zeilen in Apps und Flows repräsentiert und standardmäßig „Name“ heißt.

source.title: Table characteristics
source.quote: In Dataverse, this key is a Globally Unique Identifier (GUID), such as 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426655440000. Dataverse automatically generates the GUID when a new row is created. To improve usability, each table also includes a primary column—a readable text field used to represent rows in apps and flows.

prompt: How does Dataverse manage a many-to-many relationship, and what is true about that mechanism?

options.text: It uses a hidden intersect table that can't be edited or given custom forms
It adds a lookup column to each of the two tables that reference each other
It duplicates the associated rows in both tables and keeps them in sync
It creates two one-to-many relationships, one per direction, with lookups

explanation: Relationale Datenbanken unterstützen N:N nicht direkt. Dataverse legt dafür eine verborgene Intersect-Tabelle an, die die Zuordnungen verwaltet — sie ist nicht bearbeitbar und unterstützt keine eigenen Formulare oder Spalten. Verknüpfte Datensätze zeigt man stattdessen über ein Subgrid im Formular.

source.title: Table relationships
source.quote: Many-to-many relationships aren't directly supported by relational databases. Dataverse uses a hidden intersect table to manage these relationships. This intersect table isn't user-editable and doesn't support custom forms or columns.

prompt: For each of the following statements about Dataverse table relationships, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.text: Adding a column with the Lookup data type automatically creates a many-to-one relationship.
A many-to-one relationship is a fundamentally different relationship type from a one-to-many relationship.
In a one-to-many relationship, the referenced row is often called the parent and rows in the referencing table are the children.

explanation: Eine Lookup-Spalte erzeugt automatisch eine N:1-Beziehung. N:1 und 1:N sind dabei nicht verschieden — es ist dieselbe Beziehung aus Sicht der jeweils anderen Tabelle, eine Frage der Oberflächen-Perspektive. Die referenzierte Zeile ist der Parent, die referenzierenden Zeilen sind die Children.

source.title: Table relationships
source.quote: A common way to create a table relationship is by adding a column with the Lookup data type. This automatically creates a many-to-one relationship. The referenced row is often called the parent, while rows in the referencing table are the children. This is a matter of interface perspective, not a separate relationship type.

prompt: Service requests need a two-sentence summary of the customer's complaint that is generated automatically when the record is saved and stored in the row, so views and flows can use it without anyone typing it. Which column type meets this requirement?

options.text: A Prompt column that stores the AI-generated output of a prompt over the row's columns
A Formula column with a Power Fx expression that concatenates the description and title fields
A Rollup column that aggregates the related activity text into one summary on the request
A Multiple lines of text column filled by a scheduled flow using the Create text with GPT action

explanation: Genau dafür gibt es Prompt-Spalten: Beim Anlegen oder Ändern wertet Dataverse den Prompt gegen andere Spaltenwerte derselben Zeile aus und speichert das Ergebnis in der Spalte. Formula-Spalten können Text zusammensetzen, aber nicht zusammenfassen; Rollups aggregieren Zahlen; der Flow-Umweg ist möglich, aber weder sofortig noch nötig.

source.title: Work with Prompt columns and row summaries
source.quote: A Prompt column is an AI-powered column type in Dataverse that stores the result of a natural language prompt run against other column values in the same row. When a record is created or updated, Dataverse evaluates the prompt and stores the generated output directly in the column — ready to be used in apps, flows, or views without any manual entry.

prompt: For each of the following statements about Prompt columns, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.text: You can create up to five Prompt columns per table.
Formula columns, File columns, Image columns, and other Prompt columns can be used as input columns for a prompt.
The Copilot and AI Prompts features must be turned on in the environment's Feature settings.

explanation: Pro Tabelle sind maximal fünf Prompt-Spalten möglich. Als Eingabespalten ausgeschlossen sind Formula-, File-, Image- und andere Prompt-Spalten — ihre Werte werden ignoriert. Voraussetzung sind aktivierte Copilot- und AI-Prompts-Funktionen in den Feature settings der Umgebung.

source.title: Work with Prompt columns and row summaries
source.quote: Select + Add new prompt. You can create up to five Prompt columns per table. Input columns can't be Formula columns, File columns, Image columns, or other Prompt columns — their values are ignored if selected. Copilot and AI Prompts features must be turned on in the environment's Feature settings.

prompt: How does a row summary differ from a Prompt column?

options.text: A row summary isn't stored as a column value but generated on demand when the record is viewed
A row summary is stored in a hidden column and refreshed by a nightly system job
A row summary is configured per main form, whereas a Prompt column is configured once for the table
A row summary is refreshed when a Prompt column on the same table changes, and at no other time

explanation: Die Row Summary ist eine von Copilot erzeugte Übersicht in einer einklappbaren Leiste oben im Hauptformular oder direkt aus Ansichten. Anders als eine Prompt-Spalte wird sie nicht gespeichert, sondern beim Betrachten des Datensatzes erzeugt. Konfiguriert wird sie auf Tabellenebene und gilt dann für alle Hauptformulare und Ansichten.

source.title: Work with Prompt columns and row summaries
source.quote: A row summary is a Copilot-generated overview of a record that appears in a collapsible bar at the top of a model-driven app main form, or directly from views. Unlike a Prompt column, a row summary isn't stored as a column value — it's generated on demand when a user views the record.

prompt: Complete the statement about text column lengths in Dataverse.
textParts: The maximum length of a single line of text column is
characters, while the maximum length of a multiple lines of text column is
explanation: Single line of text fasst maximal 4.000 Zeichen (Standard 100). Multiple lines of text fasst maximal 1.048.576 Zeichen (Standard 2.000). Beide Längen lassen sich vor und nach dem Anlegen der Spalte ändern.

source.title: Column types in Microsoft Dataverse
source.quote: The maximum length of a single line of text column is 4,000 characters. The default length is 100 characters. The maximum length of multiple lines of text column is 1,048,576 characters. The default length is 2,000 characters.

prompt: Why does the guidance recommend using the Float data type only when necessary?

options.text: Float stores only an approximation, and features such as calculated columns don't support it
Float values are stored exactly but consume twice the storage space of an equivalent Decimal
Float columns don't allow the maker to configure minimum and maximum values
Float columns aren't accepted as inputs to business rules or as view columns

explanation: Float speichert nur eine Näherung des Wertes, und mehrere Dataverse-Funktionen — etwa berechnete Spalten — unterstützen Float nicht. Decimal speichert dagegen bis zu 10 Nachkommastellen exakt so, wie angegeben.

source.title: Column types in Microsoft Dataverse
source.quote: You should only use float when necessary as floating point numbers store a close approximation of the value and several Dataverse features don't support float such as calculated columns.

prompt: An organization integrates Dataverse with an external system that identifies records by its own order number rather than a GUID. Which Dataverse feature addresses this?

options.text: An alternate key on the order number column
An autonumber column with a date prefix
A rollup column on the related order table
A business rule on the order number

explanation: Ein Alternate Key identifiziert Datensätze über eine für Nutzer aussagekräftige Spalte. Dataverse erzwingt dafür Pflicht und Eindeutigkeit — Duplikate lassen sich nicht speichern. Das hilft besonders bei der Integration mit Fremdsystemen und verbessert Suche und Filterung, weil Alternate-Key-Spalten immer indiziert sind.

source.title: Create an alternate key
source.quote: When you define a column as a key, Dataverse makes sure that every entry in that key column is required and unique so you can use the key column to distinctively identify a specific record. It also improves the search and filtering on the particular column because alternate key fields are always indexed.

prompt: Purchase orders must be numbered PO-5000, PO-5001, and so on. A maker creates an autonumber column with the prefix PO, but the first saved record receives PO-1000. What should the maker change?

options.text: Set the autonumber column's seed value to 5000 in the column properties
Switch the format from String prefixed number to Date prefixed number
Recreate the column as Single line of text and enforce the number with a business rule
Create 4,000 placeholder records so the sequence advances to 5000

explanation: Der Seed ist die Startzahl des Nummernteils; Autonumber-Spalten beginnen standardmäßig bei 1000. Ein eigener Seed von 5000 liefert PO-5000 als ersten Wert. Das Datumsformat ändert das Präfix, nicht den Startwert.

source.title: Create an auto numbering column
source.quote: Autonumber columns have a default seed value of 1000, but you can set a custom seed value if you want.

prompt: For each of the following statements about Dataverse auditing, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.text: Auditing can be configured at three levels: environment, table, and column.
Column-level auditing works even when environment-level auditing is disabled.
You need the System Administrator or System Customizer role to enable or disable auditing.

explanation: Auditing ist auf drei Ebenen konfigurierbar: Umgebung, Tabelle, Spalte. Die Ebenen bauen aufeinander auf — Tabellen-Auditing setzt Umgebungs-Auditing voraus, Spalten-Auditing beides. Zum Ein- oder Ausschalten braucht es die Rolle System Administrator oder System Customizer (oder gleichwertige Rechte).

source.title: Dataverse auditing
source.quote: Auditing can be configured at three levels: environment, table, and column. Table-level auditing requires that environment-level auditing be enabled. Column-level auditing requires that both environment-level and table-level auditing be enabled. You must have the System Administrator or System Customizer role—or equivalent permissions—to enable or disable auditing.

prompt: Which statement about virtual tables in Dataverse is correct?

options.text: Data stays in the source application and isn't duplicated, yet full CRUD is supported
Source data is copied into Dataverse on a nightly schedule and updated from there afterwards
Virtual tables are read-only and don't take part in relationships with native Dataverse tables
Virtual tables support read and update operations but not create or delete on the source

explanation: Virtuelle Tabellen lassen die Daten in der Quellanwendung — sie werden nicht nach Dataverse dupliziert — und unterstützen dennoch vollständige CRUD-Operationen direkt auf den Quelldaten. Sie können außerdem an Beziehungen zu nativen wie zu anderen virtuellen Tabellen teilnehmen.

source.title: Dual-write vs. virtual tables
source.quote: By design, virtual table data remains in the source application and isn't duplicated in Dataverse. Full CRUD capabilities are supported directly on the source data.

prompt: A company runs Dynamics 365 finance and operations apps alongside Dataverse-based customer engagement apps. Changes made in either system must appear in the other in near real time, in a tightly coupled, bidirectional integration that also supports offline scenarios. Which capability fits?

options.text: Dual-write between finance and operations apps and Dataverse
Virtual tables exposing the finance and operations data in Dataverse
Two scheduled cloud flows copying changed rows in each direction
A Power Query dataflow that refreshes the Dataverse tables every hour

explanation: Dual-write ist die eingebaute, eng gekoppelte bidirektionale Integration zwischen Finance-and-Operations-Apps und Dataverse mit nahezu Echtzeit-Synchronisierung, online wie offline. Virtuelle Tabellen duplizieren keine Daten — sie zeigen sie nur; Flows und Dataflows sind weder Echtzeit noch eng gekoppelt.

source.title: Dual-write vs. virtual tables
source.quote: Dual-write is a built-in integration feature that provides near-real-time synchronization between customer engagement apps and finance and operations apps. Dual-write delivers tightly coupled, bidirectional integration between finance and operations apps and Dataverse.
